title: Prospecting Microbial Strains for Bioremediation and Probiotics Development for Metaorganism Research and Preservation
protocol: Take coordinates and temperature at sampling sites.
Collect 500 mL samples of water from each targeted site in triplicate using sterile bottles with screw caps.
Store water samples at room temperature if processing immediately after collection.
Keep water samples at 4 °C if processing later.
Cut coral fragments from the same sampling site as the water samples using a sterile pair of pliers.
Wear sterile gloves to avoid contamination when handling corals.
Rinse sampled coral fragment with 20 mL sterile saline solution or artificial seawater.
Place each coral fragment into a sterile 250−500 mL container with a screw cap containing sterile saline solution using forceps.
Weigh 5 g of coral fragments using sterile 100 mm x 20 mm Petri dishes on a weighing scale.
Transfer the weighed coral sample to a sterile mortar.
Macerate the coral sample using a sterile pestle.
Transfer the macerated sample to a sterile culture flask containing 45 mL of 3% NaCl sterile solution and 10−15 glass beads of 5 mm using a sterile spatula.
Wash the sterile mortar with some of the 45 mL sterile saline solution to recover maximum amount of macerate.
Keep the flasks under constant agitation at 150 x g for 16 hours at the water temperature of the sampling site.
Perform serial dilutions up to 10-9 in sterile saline solution for coral samples.
Pipette dilutions up and down 5x before discarding the tip.
Vortex samples for 5 s every time before performing the next serial dilution.
Pipette 100 µL of each dilution on Petri dishes containing 3% NaCl lysogeny broth (LB) agar medium.
Incubate the plates for 1−3 days at the target temperature (e.g., 26 °C).
Check the plates once a day.
Select and isolate the colonies presenting distinct growth morphologies on new plates using the streak plate technique.
Repeat this step as many times as needed to have pure colonies growing on the plates.
Store isolates at 4 °C or in glycerol if not continued immediately to subsequent steps.
Pick single colonies from the fresh plate or from the plates stored at 4 °C.
Inoculate them independently into 2 mL of sterile LB medium.
Place tubes under constant agitation (150 x g) at 24−28 °C overnight (ON).
Add 1 mL of bacterial cultures and sterile glycerol to a final concentration of 20% in cryovials.
Leave the cryovials ON at 4 °C.
Store glycerol bacterial stocks at -80 °C until needed.
Activate isolates in LB broth or alternative media by picking a single colony from fresh plates or 4 °C stored plates.
Inoculate 2 mL of sterile LB medium with the picked colony.
If using a glycerol stock, streak it on LB agar plates and incubate at 24−28 °C overnight to have single colonies growing.
Place the tube containing LB medium inclined under constant agitation (150 x g) at 24−28 °C overnight for bacterial growth.
Pellet cells by centrifuging them at 8,000 x g for 8 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant and gently pipette up and down to resuspend cells in an equal volume (2 mL) of saline water to wash remaining LB broth.
Repeat washing step twice with saline solution to ensure no traces of carbon source remain.
Inoculate washed and resuspended cells in minimum Bushnell Haas culture medium (BH Broth) containing EE2 as the only carbon source.
Dissolve EE2 in ethanol at a final concentration of 5 mg/L in the culture medium.
Assess bacterial growth by optical density at 600 nm and/or colonies forming units (CFU) on LB agar medium for 16−72 h of incubation.
Add 1−2% crude oil to 500 mL of sterile distilled water.
Agitate the mixture at 24−28 °C at 150 x g for 48 h.
Separate soluble and insoluble fraction after agitation by allowing settling for 10−20 min.
Transfer the oWSF to a new sterile flask, saving the oWIF.
Using all recovered oWSF (~400 mL), prepare 1 L of BH agar minimum medium containing oWSF as the only carbon source.
Prepare 1 L of BH agar minimum medium containing oWIF as the only carbon source using the remaining fraction from step 3.1.4.
Dilute water and coral macerate samples up to 10-6 in sterile saline solution for isolation purposes.
Pipette 100 µL of each dilution on Petri dishes containing BH-oWSF and BH-oWIF agar media.
Plate them.
Extract and sequence the DNA for taxonomic identification.
Activate isolates stocked in glycerol as described in step 2.3.1.
Extract the DNA using a DNA extraction kit.
Use primers 27f (5′-AGA GTT TGA TCA TGG CTC AG-3′) and 1492r (5′-GTT TAC CTT GTT ACG ACT T-3′).
Perform 50 µL PCR reactions according to the protocol.
Include negative controls for blank DNA extractions and PCR reactions without template DNA.
Set up a first denaturation cycle at 94 °C for 4 min.
Repeat 35 cycles at 94 °C for 1 min, followed by 50 °C for 1 min, and 72 °C for 2.5 min.
Perform a final extension cycle for 10 min at 72 °C.
Check amplicon integrity in 1.2% agarose gel using 80 V.
Gel purify the samples using a gel purification kit.
Quantify PCR products using a fluorometer.
Activate isolates in glycerol stocks from step 2.2.5 as described in step 2.3.1 but using 5 mL instead of 2 mL.
Add 1% (v/v) of the grown 5 mL culture from step 4.2.1 in triplicates to a 250 mL flask containing 100 mL of 3% LB media.
Prepare triplicates of a negative control (no inoculum).
Place flasks in an incubator under constant agitation (150 x g) at 24−28 °C.
Take 1 mL aliquots every 4 h for 48 h.
Measure optical density (OD) estimation at 600 nm wavelength and colony forming units (CFU) counted from serial dilutions plated on rich media plates.
Plot the OD and CFU curves and analyze the correlation of OD/CFU of each individual strain.
Calculate the number of cells based on the OD values.
Activate isolates as described in step 2.3.1 for antagonism test.
Inoculate one microbial strain along the middle of plates containing agar media.
Inoculate other strains perpendicular to the central inoculated strain.
Repeat the process until every selected microbial strain is tested against all others.
Incubate the plates at 24−28 °C and monitor them daily.
Observe potential halos indicating antagonistic activity between two strains.
Exclude one of the strains if halos are observed.
Activate isolates as described in step 2.3.1.
Pellet the cells at 3,500 x g.
Gently wash the cells twice with an equal volume of saline solution.
Resuspend the washed cells in an equal final volume of saline solution.
Inoculate 1 mL of culture into 100 mL of 3% NaCl LB medium.
Incubate overnight at 150 x g.
Inoculate the grown, washed, and resuspended cultures from 100 mL into 10 L cultures.
Incubate overnight in sterile air-lift bioreactors receiving filtered air from a pump.
If more culture is needed, inoculate 1% of the grown culture in fresh media.
Centrifuge the grown cultures at 8,000 x g for 8 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Wash the pellet gently by resuspending cells in 500 mL of sterile saline solution.
Repeat steps involving washing and resuspending as needed.
Resuspend each individual culture in 100 mL of saline solution.
Measure the OD to estimate the number of cells.
Calculate the volume of each culture necessary to reach a final concentration of 107 cells/mL.
Perform CFU counts on rich media for confirmation of cell viability and concentration.
Mix an equal volume of each individual culture in sterile flasks.
Aliquot the consortium into 50 mL sterile tubes.
Keep the mixture at 4 °C until inoculation.
Activate isolates from glycerol stocks by streaking them on LB agar plates.
Incubate the plates at 24−28 °C overnight to obtain single colonies.
Pick a single colony and inoculate it in 2 mL of sterile LB medium.
Place the tube with inclined LB medium under constant agitation (150 x g) at 24−28 °C overnight.
Perform DNA extraction as described for detection of potentially beneficial genes by PCR.
